summary: Alert Tagging: operators attach free-form tags to alerts (many-to-many), add/remove via API, filter GET /api/alerts by tag, and see tags in AlertResponse.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new Tag entity exists with a many-to-many relationship to Alert, persisted via a new join table and a new EF migration (database/ migration script regenerated).
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags to the alert and returns the updated alert including its tags; returns 404 if the alert does not exist.
POST dedupes tags case-insensitively, both within the request and against tags already on the alert (no duplicate assignment).
An alert may have at most 10 tags; a POST that would result in more than 10 is rejected with 400 and changes nothing.
Each tag must be 1-30 characters; an empty/whitespace-only or longer tag is rejected with 400.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes the tag assignment (204); returns 404 if the alert or the tag assignment does not exist.
GET /api/alerts accepts an optional 'tag' query parameter and returns only alerts that have that tag.
The 'tag' filter composes (AND) with the existing filters isActive, severity, createdFrom/createdTo and search, and with paging/sorting/TotalCount.
AlertResponse includes the alert's tags (empty list when none) on all endpoints that return an alert.

constraints: Controllers stay HTTP-only; tag rules (dedupe, max 10, trim) live in AlertManagementService; EF access only in AlertService.Data.SQL behind IAlertRepository.
Do not change behavior of existing endpoints beyond adding the optional 'tag' filter and a 'tags' field on AlertResponse (additive, non-breaking).

Database naming: PascalCase tables/columns; index IX_[Table]_[Columns]; PK/FK per database standard (e.g. IX_Tags_Name unique). Join table and index must be created through an EF migration; regenerate database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql.
Tag filter must use parameterized EF/LINQ (no raw SQL); avoid N+1 by Include/projection when loading tags for list results.
Validate tag input at the API boundary (length 1-30, non-whitespace, max 10 per alert); tag value in DELETE route is URL-encoded user input.
Max tags per alert (10) and tag length (30) defined as constants in AlertConstants, not magic numbers.
coverage_goals: Behavior coverage of AC1-AC9: dedupe, 10-tag limit, 1-30 length, 404 paths, tag filter composed with each existing filter, tags in response.

findings.description: GetByIdAsync now tracks the alert with its Tags, and the existing UpdateAsync calls _context.Alerts.Update(alert). DbSet.Update traverses the reachable graph and marks every reachable entity with a key (the loaded Tag rows) as Modified, so UpdateAsync/DeactivateAsync on a tagged alert issue unnecessary UPDATE statements against shared Tags rows.
findings.reason: Unintended side effect on existing update/deactivate paths: extra writes to shared Tag rows (contention risk) introduced by the tag change; not caught by the SQLite tests because values are unchanged.
findings.suggestion: In UpdateAsync mark only the alert as modified (e.g. _context.Entry(alert).State = EntityState.Modified, or rely on change tracking and just SaveChangesAsync) so the Tags graph is not marked Modified; keep the change minimal.

Tag character set restrictions (e.g. allowed characters, '/' handling in DELETE route): NOT_SPECIFIED.
unresolved_questions: Assumed (confirm): POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags returns 200 OK with the updated AlertResponse (tags are added to an existing alert, not a new top-level resource). Alternative: 201/204.
Assumed (confirm): a POST whose deduped result would exceed 10 tags is rejected entirely with 400 (no partial add); tags already on the alert do not count as new.
Assumed (confirm): tags are trimmed before validation; the first-seen casing is stored and displayed; matching (dedupe, GET filter, DELETE) is case-insensitive.
Assumed (confirm): re-adding a tag already on the alert is idempotent (no error). POST with an empty tags array returns 400.
Assumed (confirm): tags are shared entities (unique by name) and are not deleted when their last alert assignment is removed (no orphan cleanup in this story).
Assumed (confirm): the tag filter accepts a single tag value (not a list) and a non-existent tag simply yields an empty page.
Assumed (confirm): deleting an alert also removes its tag assignments (join rows cascade) but not the Tag rows.
